name: Restaurant Menu with Allergen Labels, QR Code & Table Reservations
author: Rebel Studios Software

sections.description:
Everything a restaurant needs on its WordPress site, done simply:

Free

  • A polished menu: add dishes with price, description, photo and dietary tags, grouped into sections (Starters, Mains, Desserts…). Show it anywhere with [rsres_menu].
  • Allergen and dietary labels: each dish takes a short label of your own (vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, V, GF, contains nuts), separated by commas or slashes and shown as badges under the dish. You write the labels, so they say what your kitchen actually does: there is no allergen database, no filtering the menu by allergen, and nothing here checks your wording against your local labelling rules.
  • Table reservations: a clean booking form ([rsres_reservation]) with date, time, party size and notes. The guest gets a confirmation email; you get a notification and can confirm or cancel from the admin, which emails the guest. It is a request book, not a floor plan: nothing here counts your tables, so two parties can both ask for 8pm and every booking waits for your yes.
  • A printable QR code menu: a QR code that opens your menu page on a guest’s phone. That is a contactless menu with no app to install, no per-table fee and no third-party service in the middle: print it and put it on the tables.
  • No monthly fees, nothing phones home — the QR is generated on your own server.

Who it is for

Anywhere with a menu — a door is optional. A bistro or a diner that wants the same menu on the wall
and on a phone. A pizzeria taking Friday bookings. A deli or a coffee shop whose short list changes
on Monday. A sushi counter where the seats are the whole constraint and every booking needs your
yes. A brewery or a winery where the tap list or the wine list is the offer. A pub. A food truck
with no dining room at all, whose menu lives on a QR sticker and changes with the pitch. A catering
kitchen publishing next month’s menu before anyone asks for it.

None of that needs different software. It needs a menu you can edit, a QR code for the tables, and
somewhere for people to book.

Pro

Pro adds online ordering for pickup and delivery with order-ahead times, and reservation deposits, both paid through your own WooCommerce checkout — your gateway, your money, and no percentage of your orders. $69 a year or $207 once, with a 7-day money-back guarantee.

What Pro does not add, stated plainly: no table management or floor plan, no WhatsApp order routing, and no driver dispatch or delivery tracking. If one of those is what you need, this is not the product.

Other plugins by Rebel Studios

Focused WooCommerce plugins that each do one job well:

  • Rebel Studios Event Tickets & QR Check-in: events, RSVP and QR tickets you scan at the door.
  • Rebel Studios Membership & Content Restriction: restrict content to members, with front-end registration.
  • Invoice Documents for WooCommerce: automatic PDF invoices, packing slips and delivery notes.
  • Brazilian Checkout Fields for WooCommerce: CPF/CNPJ validation and CEP autofill for Brazilian stores.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate. A Restaurant menu appears.
  2. Add menu sections and items (with prices and photos).
  3. Create a page with the [rsres_menu] shortcode, and another with [rsres_reservation].
  4. Under Restaurant → Settings, set your name, notification email and pick your Menu page to generate the QR code.
sections.faq:
Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Menu, reservations and the QR menu are standalone. WooCommerce is only used by Pro for paid online ordering.

How do I get the QR code menu, and can I print it big?

Pick your menu page under Restaurant → Settings and save. The code appears on that screen,
pointing at the page that holds your food menu. There is no download button: save the image out of
your browser (right-click → Save image as) or print the settings page. It is drawn on your own
server, so nothing expires and no account can switch it off — but it is a plain black-and-white PNG
about 200 pixels square, which is right for a table card and soft if you blow it up to a poster.
There is no SVG or PDF export, no logo in the middle, no colour, and no scan counting. One code
covers the whole menu page; there are no per-table codes. Change that page’s address later and the
cards you already printed still point at the old one, so reprint them.

How do reservations work?

Guests submit a request; you get an email and see it in Restaurant → Reservations, where you confirm or cancel. Confirming emails the guest automatically. That screen holds the 200 most recent bookings.

Does it stop two parties booking the same table?

No, and that is the main thing to know before you install it. It takes requests; it does not keep a floor plan. Nothing counts your tables, holds one, or blocks a second party asking for the same 7:00 pm. Every booking lands as Pending and waits for you to confirm or cancel — you are the availability check. If you need software that knows a table is already taken, this is not that plugin.

Can I set opening hours, or bookable time slots?

Not as rules. Hours / note on form prints a line of your own text above the form (Tue–Sat, 5–10pm), and the time field still accepts whatever a guest types, so a request can arrive for 3am on a Monday you are shut. You decline it like any other. There are no slots, no closed days and no per-slot limit. The one hard limit is Max party size (12 unless you change it), which sets how far the Party dropdown counts.

Can a guest change or cancel their own booking?

No. There is no link in the email and nothing on the front end, so a booking cannot be touched once it is sent. Replies to the guest emails go to your reservation address, so the guest asks you and you make the change in Restaurant → Reservations. Confirming, cancelling and reinstating a cancelled booking each email the guest.

The reservation emails are not arriving.

They go out through WordPress’s own mail (wp_mail) as plain text. This plugin adds no mail
service, no API key and no SMTP settings of its own, so if your host does not send mail reliably,
neither do these — an SMTP plugin pointed at your own mailbox fixes that, and is the usual cure for
them landing in spam, because they are sent from WordPress’s default address with only a
Reply-To set to your reservation address. Check one setting first: your own notification is sent
only if Reservation notifications to holds a single valid address. Leave it blank, mistype it,
or put two addresses in it, and the booking still arrives in Restaurant → Reservations but nothing
emails you — the guest still gets their email, though their replies then go to WordPress’s default
address instead of yours. There is no calendar invite and no SMS.

Can I show allergens on the menu?

Each menu item has a dietary tags field. Whatever you type — vegan, vegetarian, gluten-free, dairy-free, V, GF, contains nuts — is shown as a badge under that dish, split on commas, slashes or pipes. It is a label you control, not a database: the plugin does not know which ingredients contain which allergens, cannot filter the menu by allergen, and does not check your wording against local labelling rules.

Can I reorder the sections, or the dishes inside one?

Sections print in the order you created them — make Starters first and it stays first — and there is no drag handle to reshuffle them afterwards. Inside a section, dishes come out alphabetically by name. The menu does honour menu_order if a post-ordering plugin sets it, but nothing in this plugin writes it. [rsres_menu] takes no attributes either, so it always prints the whole menu — there is no section="Drinks". Each section does get its own URL under /menu-section/, but that page is your theme’s archive list, not the priced menu layout.

I used [rs_menu] and the page shows the text instead of my menu.

Rename it to [rsres_menu] (and [rs_reservation] to [rsres_reservation]). Version 1.1 renamed both shortcodes to carry the plugin’s own prefix, as the directory requires, and this readme went on giving the old names for longer than it should have. Sorry — it is a one-word edit on your page, and nothing else changed.

Who can see reservations?

Editors and Administrators. Bookings hold guests’ names, emails, phone numbers and notes, and confirming or cancelling emails the guest, so Authors and Contributors can’t open the Reservations screen or change a booking. If your floor staff use another role, give it the capability you want with the rsres_staff_capability filter (it returns edit_others_posts by default).

If I delete the plugin, does it take my menu with it?

No. Uninstalling deletes one row, the plugin’s settings. Your menu items, sections and reservations are ordinary posts and stay in the database, so a reinstall finds them all again. They do stop being visible anywhere while the plugin is gone, which is worth knowing before you delete it to troubleshoot something else.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • Changed: QR codes are now generated with bacon/bacon-qr-code (BSD-2-Clause) instead of chillerlan/php-qrcode. The previous library carries ZXing-derived files under Apache-2.0, which is not compatible with GPLv2. No change to the codes themselves.

1.1.1

  • Security: the Reservations screen and confirming or cancelling a booking now need an Editor or Administrator. Before, any Contributor could read every guest’s name, email, phone and notes, and confirm or cancel bookings, which emails the guest.
  • Developer: rsres_staff_capability filter.

1.1.0

  • Improvement: redesigned menu (section headings, “Chef’s pick” badges, one tag per dietary label) and reservation card.
  • Fix: reservation fields no longer overlap or overflow the card on themes that don’t set box-sizing.
  • Fix: items without a price no longer show a dotted leader to nowhere.
  • Improvement: Reservations can be filtered by status (with counts), read as “Mon, Sep 21, 7:00 pm”, sort by table time with upcoming first, and offer only the changes that apply, including Reinstate for a cancelled booking.
  • Fix: the Reservations screen now loads the plugin’s admin styles.

1.0.1

  • Fix: reservations could be requested for dates that had already passed.
  • Fix: menu items without a price showed “$0.00”; they now show no price.
  • Improvement: with WooCommerce active, the menu uses the store’s currency symbol unless you set one, and follows it if the store currency changes later.
  • Improvement: the stylesheet now loads only on pages with the menu or reservation form.
  • Fix: cancelling a reservation now emails the guest (only confirming did), and changing a status twice no longer emails twice.
  • Fix: a booking that arrives already confirmed (a paid deposit in Pro) no longer tells the guest “we will confirm shortly”.
  • Improvement: guests can reply to reservation emails and reach the restaurant’s reservation address.

1.0.0

  • Initial release: menu, table reservations with email confirmation, and a printable QR menu.
